title: Where to find great short films?

commenti.body: [removed]

On the Criterion Channel, I'd highly recommend the short documentaries of Vittorio de Seta (not de Sica). I truly enjoyed all of them; they offer a look at a then-vanishing (and now almost entirely vanished) rural southern Italy. Martin Scorsese has described de Seta as "an anthropologist who speaks with the voice of a poet."

Speaking of Scorsese, the Criterion Channel also has a retrospective of Scorsese's shorts.

Short avant-garde films on YouTube I'd recommend:

[The Dante Quartet by Stan Brakhage](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=804VpE7YARU)

[Black Ice by Stan Brakhage](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5VXOYYXBCck)

[The Girl Chewing Gum by John Smith](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCZTqrsYN6A&t=119s)

[Associations by John Smith](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FfWjDnDg4-s)

[An Optical Poem by Oskar Fischinger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FcHsysPGSt0) 

Are you interest in more mainstream animation? If so, I'd definitely recommend the classic thirties Disney shorts, especially *The Old Mill*.

And, of course, there are the classic, pioneering films of the Lumière brothers and George Méliès, which have been in the public domain for a long time and are thus widely available online.

I hope this helps and that you find at least one of these suggestions enjoyable.

Check Letterboxd for lists of what you can find on YouTube. Quite a lot of independent filmmakers upload their films to Vimeo but you may have to pay for some. MUBI might be the best example of what you’re looking for as it has a lot of shorts from established directors, but you’re have to pay for it.

I recommend you a series of comedy short films "The Road", telling about the funny adventures of road masters, shot in Soviet Georgia according to the script by Rezo Gabriadze.

A total of nine films were released (from 1974 to 1980), and each of them is a true masterpiece. We have no doubt that many of you perfectly remember the simple and funny adventures of three road workers, convincingly and brilliantly played by famous Georgian actors.

Rezo Gabriadze was the author of scripts for full-length films that left a noticeable mark on Soviet cinema.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=\_VRBS9BEvzc

Ubu (UbuWeb) hosts an extensive open library of experimental film, audio and texts. Some of it is of questionable quality (some of the Markopoulos films for instance, but I guess getting them in decent quality at all is a challenge) but it more than makes up for it in ease of access and extensive coverage. Worth noting is that their focus is hosting things that are not readily available elsewhere.

I believe all of Kenneth Anger's films are there, as is the case with Marie Menken's shorts. However, as their focus is primarily on hosting things that are not readily available elsewhere, they're a bit sparse on people like Brakhage and Maya Deren, who's films have seen a wider distribution. It's an excellent research, and a good first place to go for experimental filmmakers.

Most of the major PT Anderson movies have had an accompanying short movie made of unused footage from the main movie (eg Blossoms and Blood accompanies Punch Drunk Love, For the Hungry Boy accompanies Phantom Thread). They're all worth watching. You might also want to watch Coffee & Cigarettes, which was the short film test for Hard Eight, his full length debut.

You need to be more specific, short films come in a variety of shapes and forms... From experimental to mainstream melodrama.

A good start is to look for the Oscars shortlist of every year. And I'm thinking of one in particular : Ryan (Chris Landreth) on YT. Or Two Distant Strangers (Free+Roe) on Netflix.

You can find lots of shorts on the [Arte channel](https://www.arte.tv/fr/videos/cinema/courts-metrages/) (Franco-German). [Bref](https://www.brefcinema.com/) (also French). [Sofy](https://sofy.tv/) (English but paying)

[Requiem](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UU5WUc2KhKc&t=709s) starring Bella Ramsey is great 

My favourite short is this one by Bi Gan who went on to direct Kaili Blues and Long Day's Journey Into Night - [Secret Goldfish](https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x7p4b8s) - so short with a run time of 1.5 mins and so beautiful

I would also recommend watching good anthology films like Mystery Train, Night on Earth, Wild Tales - and imagine them as standalone shorts as these are well executed 20\~ min segments with often simple concepts

I am a big fan of *Salón Royale*, which should be on Youtube with English subtitles.

It's a "professional" short film with real actors, not some amateur stuff.  
Its basic ingredients are simply three young women in a car, talking. The first part of the short film takes place while they are driving to a party, the second part while they are returning from that party. It's all in the dialogue and what is and isn't said.
